transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-19
Start: 10:00 PT | Duration: ~67 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh, Marcus Lee, Sofia Ramos, Diego Alvarez + all-staff dial-in

Summary:
Ava opened with company priorities (reliability, cost controls, Private availability), Priya walked through Q2 product cadence, Marcus covered ops and recent incidents, Liam gave a tech signal on performance and private deployment readiness, Sofia gave a short research update on quantization and evals. Q&A focused on Dedicated vs Hosted economics, SOC2/audit timelines, and on-call/incident expectations. Several action items and owners assigned.

Topics covered:
- Q2 roadmap and product cadence
- Reliability & incident recap
- Private/VPC progress and enterprise enablement
- Performance benchmarks and model/quantization signals
- People & hiring priorities

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava: Good morning everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off the spring crew signal, um, quick housekeeping, recording is on, please keep mics muted unless you're speaking.
[00:22] Marcus: Quick note, we've got about an hour, 10, so lots to cover. I'll start with operational highlights then hand off.
[00:31] Marcus: Last two weeks we had two notable incidents, one was a region failover that exposed a mis- configured autoscale policy, the other was a memory leak in a legacy variant that caused degraded latency. Both were contained, no customer data exposure.
[00:45] Priya: Can you just restate the timeline so folks understand severity?
[00:50] Marcus: Sure, incident one - 03/03, we lost a AZ in us-west-2, traffic rerouted, some warm containers didn't scale fast enough, about 12 minutes of elevated latencies for a subset of hosted customers. We failed over to Dedicated pool for two enterprise tenants per our fallback policy.
[01:12] Marcus: Incident two - 03/10, memory pressure with a model variant during long-context evals, GC thrash, we rolled a hotfix within 45 minutes. Post-incident we bumped observability retention and added more KV cache metrics.
[01:38] Ava: Thanks Marcus. The point I want to land is we are investing in more deterministic failovers and clearer playbooks — this is a reliability-first quarter.
[01:48] Liam: On the tech side, we shipped a new batching optimizer that reduced tail latency for short sequences by about 15% in our internal canaries. This is the kernel selection work we mentioned last quarter.
[02:05] Liam: Caveat, the gains are workload-dependent; long-context workloads didn't see the same uplift due to kv cache thrash, so we have follow-ups.
[02:18] Sofia: We ran quantization experiments on two open models, 4-bit q4 and an int8 path, the quality regressions were modest for embeddings and prompt completions, but for some structured-code outputs we saw a delta. We'll publish the detailed evals.
[02:35] Priya: Framings on product — Q2 focus: 1) hardened Private release (VPC + KMS integrations), 2) rollout of Optimize suggestions as an early-access feature, 3) better pricing transparency in Console.
[02:56] Priya: On Private: we've closed the integration for one large customer in EMEA for KMS, remaining items are onboarding docs, audit logs, and a final security sign-off.
[03:10] Audience (All): applause / clapping sounds (inaudible)
[03:20] Diego: People update - hiring pace steady, we prioritized SRE hires and two product managers. New coaching program for managers starts next month.
[03:36] Ava: Quick financial signpost — run rate unchanged vs last month, usage growth in hosted slowed but Dedicated commitments increased. This aligns with our thesis that customers move to Dedicated as they scale.
[03:54] Ava: We're also tightening cost controls — expect new quota guardrails for some free tier endpoints to manage noise.
[04:04] Liam: Back to technical, a couple of detail points: the Private/VPC package now supports SAML SSO, but we have to finalize audit log formats for ISO/SOC ingestion. The security team flagged schema expectations with some customers.
[04:25] Marcus: On the reliability roadmap, immediate items: surge scaling runbook, more aggressive canarying on model rollouts, and an automated fallback policy for incompatible model variants.
[04:40] Priya: On product rollouts, we will start canary A/Bs with a subset of internal product teams for Optimize suggestions next week. You'll get invites.
[04:51] [05:00] Q&A session opens
[05:00] Speaker 1 (Engineer from infra): Question — can you share more about the fallback policy, how transparent will it be in Console?
[05:12] Marcus: Good question. The plan is to expose a visible fallback trace in the Console and alerting when requests are routed to a cheaper or compatible variant. That will include model id, variant, and reason code.
[05:28] Speaker 2 (AE in sales): Will that show up in cost breakdowns per token?
[05:32] Priya: Yes, cost and latency attribution will be per-route and per-model in the next Console patch.
[05:41] [06:00] Speaker mislabeled (Speaker 3): Is SOC2 timing still Q3?
[06:05] Ava: We are on track for a Type II in Q3; security has the audit plan, but realize we will have pre-audit scoping with customers that need SOC2 earlier.
[06:18] Sofia: Small note — for some of the quantization work, the evals need domain-specific prompt sets; if teams have customer prompts they want tested, please share.
[06:31] Liam: We also have a performance ask — Marcus and I want to run model throughput benchmarks in staging with actual customer-like load. We'll schedule a benchmark week.
[06:44] Priya: On pricing transparency, we want to provide clearer levers for customers: per-model quantization discounts, Dedicated reservation pricing examples, and a calculator in Console to show cost implications.
[07:03] Diego: People question — what are expectations for all-hands participation? We want to keep them inclusive but not mandatory for every meeting; team leads will decide core attendees.
[07:18] Ava: For the leadership ask: we need top-down clarity on hiring by the end of the month. Prioritize SRE, a product manager for Optimize, and one reliability engineer for Private.
[07:34] [08:00] Marcus: Ops retrospective — we learned a lot from the AZ failover. Specific items: fix autoscale warm policies, add synthetic traffic to detect scaling regressions, and a new alert for KV eviction spikes.
[08:20] Marcus: Also, patch management cadence — we'll push a more predictable weekly security patch window to reduce surprise rollouts.
[08:33] [09:00] Technical deep dive highlight (Liam): Kernel selection improvement notes — misspellings in telemetry made analysis harder, we standardized event names. This reduced noise.
[09:10] Liam: The optimizer is conservative by default; we'll release a more aggressive tuning for Dedicated customers who opt-in.
[09:22] [10:00] Sofia: On research timelines — we have a short list of experiments: wider q4 int8 path, prefix-kv caching heuristics, and a prompt-eval suite for hallucination regression. Expect interim results in 2-3 weeks.
[10:38] [12:00] Audience question (product): Are there plans to support on-prem air-gapped installations?
[12:07] Priya: Yes, that's in Private roadmap as an enterprise option; timelines depend on compliance gating and legal/contracting. We'll need a pilot customer to validate distribution.
[12:25] [14:00] Marcus: Incident escalation reminder — follow the new incident commander rotation, please update the rota if you can't make your on-call week. We want clear handoffs.
[14:40] [17:00] Priya: Roadmap highlight again — product will split Optimize into an EA cohort for customers, and then GA in Q4, aiming to move some customers from manual tuning to automated suggestions over time.
[17:29] Ava: Quick company priorities call-out: Reliability (top), Private readiness, and sustainable growth — that order hasn't changed.
[17:45] [20:00] Short break in recording noise / side chatter (murmurs)
[20:30] Liam: On the quantization items, a note on hallucination for structured outputs — we observed a 3-4% increase in incorrect tokens for a small test set when moving to 4-bit without additional calibration. We'll pair model-level regression alerts with quality checks.
[21:05] Sofia: We'll add regression thresholds into the eval pipeline. Teams should own model-specific test prompts for their use-cases.
[21:27] [25:00] HR note (Diego): Company retreat in May — sign-ups open next week. Also, new manager program registration deadline is 2027-04-01.
[25:50] [28:00] Audience Q: What is the plan for Dedicated vs Hosted guidance for customers evaluating us?
[28:10] Priya: We'll publish a decision tree and cost comparison doc. For most small teams, Hosted is fastest to adopt. For predictable latency and compliance, Dedicated or Private is the recommendation. We'll include model quantization profiles in the doc.
[28:37] Marcus: Also, show expected per-token costs for various batch sizes and quantization settings — that helps sales set expectations.
[29:02] [32:00] Ava: Any blockers from Sales or Customer Success?
[32:05] Speaker 4 (Sales): Some enterprise customers are asking for HSM integrations for KMS — timeline?
[32:12] Liam: We're working with security on HSM support; it's non-trivial but prioritized for Q3. For near-term, customer-managed KMS with logs is the path.
[32:28] [35:00] Priya: Can we accelerate an FAQ for procurement teams on SLAs, data residency, and contractual items? Legal is drafting but product will help.
[35:12] Ava: Legal and Sales please collaborate — get default templates out.
[35:24] [38:00] Quick demo note (Priya): Sneak peek of the new Console lamp — cost breakdown per route and a toggle for showing fallback events. We'll demo in two weeks at a product sync.
[38:32] [41:00] Marcus: Back to reliability, experiment with synthetic load test on Fridays at 03:00 PST to validate surge policies — opt-in list will be open.
[41:20] [45:00] Questions pile-up: various quick clarifications on roadmaps, audits, and hiring; some crosstalk and people dropping off.
[45:47] [50:00] Closing notes from Ava: Thank you team — keep the learnings public, document playbooks, and own the follow-ups. We'll publish a riff of this meeting with key decisions in #all-hands-summary.
[50:30] Ava: Reminder — leadership office hours next Tuesday. Bring prioritization questions.
[51:02] [60:00] Post-meeting smaller syncs happen (not recorded in full)

Recap & explicit next steps said on call:
- Priya to publish Q2 product cadence doc and the Hosted vs Dedicated decision tree by 2027-03-24.
- Marcus to share incident retro and surge-scaling runbook by 2027-03-26.
- Liam and Marcus to schedule benchmark week for model throughput (week of 2027-03-29).
- Sofia to publish quantization evals and regression thresholds by 2027-03-30.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker attribution errors, timestamps approximate, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly ("K-V cache" as "K V cash" at times), filler words and short crosstalk not fully captured.
